chunks: From him, from Ayoub ibn Nuhr, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who travels and passes by a house he owns on the road, does he complete the prayer or shorten it? He said: 'He shortens it; it is only the house where he has settled (made his home).'

key_terms.تَوَطَّنَهُ: He has settled/made it his home

ai.seo_question: Does passing by one's own house during travel end the state of travel for prayer shortening?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential definition of 'settling' (tawattun) for the purpose of shortening prayers (qasr), establishing that mere ownership or passing by a residence does not terminate the traveler's status. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on actual residence and intent over physical presence, ensuring the traveler maintains the concession of qasr until they truly establish a home there. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, prioritizing the traveler's continuous journey over incidental stops at owned properties.
